paragraphs: Photoplethysmography, or PPG, measures changes in blood volume without invasive procedures and appears in both wearables and clinical equipment. Learning reusable representations from these signals is difficult when training depends on carefully cleaned recordings. A model trained that way may struggle with the noisier signals encountered during daily activities.

This paper uses accompanying electrocardiogram and respiratory recordings to guide PPG pretraining on ICU data. These additional physiological signals help select samples for contrastive learning, which learns representations by comparing examples. The approach retains noisy PPG segments as useful training material instead of requiring high-quality or field-like recordings.

The model improves performance on 14 of 15 downstream tasks while using three times fewer pretraining subjects than existing leading approaches. The tasks include daily activity and heart rate prediction under field-like conditions. These results support the value of complementary physiological supervision: other signals can help a PPG model learn from imperfect recordings and generalize more effectively to consumer-grade data.
icml-2026-a-robust-ppg-foundation-model-.tldr: Using accompanying heart and respiratory signals during pretraining helps a PPG foundation model learn from noisy data and improve across most evaluated tasks.

paragraphs: Normalizing flows need flexible transformations that can also be reversed. Existing scalar transformations trade off useful properties: affine maps have limited expressivity, splines are only piecewise smooth and operate on bounded domains, and residual approaches require numerical inversion. These choices affect how a flow represents a distribution and how conveniently it can be evaluated.

The paper introduces three transformation families that are smooth everywhere, operate across the entire real line, and have closed-form inverses. Used inside coupling flows, they match or exceed spline performance. The authors also build radial flows that change distance from a center while preserving direction, giving the transformation a direct geometric interpretation.

Evaluations cover one- and two-dimensional benchmarks and a higher-dimensional lattice field theory problem. For targets with radial structure, radial flows can reach comparable quality to coupling flows with 1,000 times fewer parameters. The paper also reports strong training stability and improvements over affine baselines in the physics setting, where tailored designs address mode collapse.
icml-2026-analytic-bijections-for-smooth.tldr: New analytically invertible transformations give normalizing flows global smoothness and support compact, interpretable radial architectures.

paragraphs: Repeated interactions between agents are often expected to follow a stable strategic pattern, but actual behavior can drift. This paper asks how to detect such departures while observations are still arriving. The goal is to monitor a specified behavioral benchmark without choosing the total number of observations in advance.

The method constructs a statistical process that effectively bets against the benchmark. Evidence accumulates when observed payoffs systematically conflict with the conditions that benchmark requires. Using the e-value framework makes the resulting inference valid under ongoing monitoring. For repeated normal-form games, the framework handles Nash, correlated, and coarse correlated equilibrium within one approach.

The authors provide finite-time guarantees and analyze how long detection takes. They also use multiple-testing procedures to improve detection power in large games while controlling the false discovery rate. An extension to stochastic games checks whether trajectories follow a specified target policy. Together, these results turn strategic consistency into an online statistical question, including settings where behavior depends on the current state.
icml-2026-anytime-detection-of-strategic.tldr: An anytime-valid statistical framework detects departures from equilibrium or a target policy as multi-agent interactions unfold.

paragraphs: Evaluating a pretrained audio representation is difficult when the evaluation itself changes the model. Finetuning can obscure the quality of the original features, while simple probes may fail to extract information already present. The paper identifies this problem in audio self-supervised learning, where probing can change model rankings relative to finetuning on AudioSet.

The authors introduce Convex Gated Probing, a prototype-based evaluator that draws on all frozen model layers. A gating mechanism determines how to use these layers, helping expose where task-relevant information resides. This substantially narrows the performance gap between probing and finetuning while keeping the underlying representations fixed.

The probe then serves as a guide for revising the broader training pipeline. The authors change data preprocessing, architecture, and the pretraining recipe to produce Better Audio Transformer, or BAT. They report new leading results on audio benchmarks. The contribution therefore combines a stronger way to assess existing representations with a model whose development is informed by that assessment.
icml-2026-bat-better-audio-transformer-g.tldr: A probe that combines information across frozen audio-model layers guides the development of BAT, which achieves leading audio benchmark results.

paragraphs: Bulk RNA sequencing and DNA methylation provide two kinds of biological information relevant to cancer modeling. Combining them is challenging because both contain many measurements. The paper develops a joint representation model so that downstream predictions can use information from both modalities within a shared learning framework.

Training uses masked language modeling as a self-supervised objective: the model learns from partially hidden inputs rather than relying solely on downstream outcome labels. Its architecture reduces the memory demands associated with purely transformer-based approaches to long sequences. This addresses a practical obstacle to learning from high-dimensional biological inputs.

The resulting joint embeddings support finetuned cancer-type classification and survival models. The authors report state-of-the-art performance in comparisons with unimodal models. They also introduce a learning framework that maintains downstream performance when modalities are missing. This matters for the intended clinical setting, where the usefulness of combining measurements depends partly on whether the model remains effective when a complete set is unavailable.
icml-2026-bimodal-masked-language-modeli.tldr: A memory-conscious masked modeling approach combines RNA-seq and DNA methylation for cancer prediction while supporting missing modalities.

paragraphs: Spoken language models can synthesize speech without an explicit pipeline that converts written characters into phonemes. For languages with little transcribed speech, synthetic training data supplies useful pronunciation supervision. The paper finds a trade-off: increasing reliance on synthetic speech improves phonetic accuracy but progressively reduces variation in prosody, eroding expressivity.

The authors propose two self-alignment approaches for different resource conditions. Disentanglement-Guided Self-Alignment uses the separation between prosody and vocal timbre to recover expressivity in complex languages. Temperature-Driven Self-Critique targets situations with exceptionally few authentic references, using automated exploration and filtering to stabilize generation.

The work reports performance exceeding strong commercial systems, including ElevenLabs and Gemini Pro, and claims the first zero-shot voice cloning capability for Lao. Its central finding is that expanding synthetic training data can change more than pronunciation accuracy: it can also narrow expressive behavior. The proposed alignment methods address that tension while accounting for how much authentic reference material is available.
icml-2026-bridging-the-stability-express.tldr: Two self-alignment methods address the loss of speech expressivity that can accompany synthetic-data scaling in low-resource languages.

paragraphs: Test-time guidance steers a pretrained diffusion model toward outputs favored by a reward function. For Bayesian inference, however, obtaining highly rewarded outputs is not the entire goal. Samples should follow the posterior distribution, so that the relative frequency of different possibilities reflects the inference problem rather than only their reward scores.

The paper shows that common guidance methods fail to recover this posterior and identifies structural approximations responsible for the mismatch. It then proposes alternative estimators with consistency properties that enable calibrated posterior sampling. The contribution concerns the distribution produced by guidance, extending the focus beyond whether individual outputs satisfy the steering objective.

Across the evaluated Bayesian inference tasks, the proposed approach significantly outperforms previous methods. The authors also report a new state-of-the-art peak signal-to-noise ratio for black hole image reconstruction. These findings connect the theoretical correction to improved task results: guidance designed around the posterior can support both calibrated sampling and strong reconstruction performance in the reported setting.
icml-2026-calibrated-test-time-guidance-.tldr: Consistent guidance estimators correct posterior-sampling failures in common diffusion guidance methods and improve evaluated Bayesian inference tasks.

paragraphs: A language model's usefulness in healthcare depends on more than its ability to produce fluent answers. It must also handle factual questions, demographic differences, sensitive information, and adversarial inputs across languages. The paper addresses a gap in evaluating these properties when healthcare users speak languages with differing amounts of training data.

CLINIC is a multilingual benchmark covering truthfulness, fairness, safety, robustness, and privacy. It turns these five dimensions into 18 tasks across 15 languages and a range of healthcare topics. This structure makes trustworthiness a collection of assessable capabilities, allowing evaluation to consider both language coverage and different kinds of failure.

The reported evaluation finds problems with factual correctness, bias across demographic and linguistic groups, vulnerability to privacy breaches, and susceptibility to adversarial attacks. These findings identify obstacles to broader healthcare deployment among the evaluated models. The benchmark provides a framework for studying those shortcomings across languages, so progress can be assessed beyond performance in the high-resource languages that dominate model training.
icml-2026-clinic-evaluating-multilingual.tldr: CLINIC evaluates healthcare language models across 15 languages and reveals weaknesses in factuality, fairness, privacy, and resistance to attacks.

paragraphs: A piecewise stationary bandit problem contains periods of stable reward behavior separated by changes. A learner must choose actions while dealing with those changes, without necessarily knowing when they will occur. This paper introduces Detection Augmented Learning, or DAL, to handle that setting without prior knowledge of the underlying non-stationarity.

DAL combines a change detector with an existing stationary bandit algorithm. The input algorithm must have order-optimal regret, meaning its performance loss has the appropriate optimal scaling for its stationary problem. Treating that algorithm as a black box makes the framework broadly reusable across common bandit variants, rather than requiring a separate learning method for every variant.

Experiments cover synthetic benchmarks and real-world datasets with diverse non-stationary behavior. The authors report that DAL consistently surpasses the state-of-the-art methods in those evaluations and provide theoretical insights into its performance. The approach matters because it connects established stationary learners with explicit change detection, offering a general route to adapting them to environments that change in stages.
icml-2026-dal-a-practical-prior-free-bla.tldr: DAL equips order-optimal stationary bandit algorithms with change detection to handle unknown shifts in reward behavior.

paragraphs: Video predictors can provide useful dynamics knowledge for systems that connect vision, language, and action. Yet predicting a broadly plausible future does not necessarily capture the precise changes needed for manipulation. Small visual prediction errors can be amplified when a downstream policy uses those predictions to choose actions.

Dyn-VPP addresses this through post-training of diffusion predictors. It treats the sequence of denoising steps as a policy to optimize and uses a verifiable terminal reward to align predicted future latent representations with expert visual dynamics. The method leaves the architecture unchanged while explicitly training for dynamics signals that likelihood-oriented learning may miss.

Experiments in varied simulated and real-world manipulation settings show improved consistency of visual dynamics and consistently higher task success. These results connect better future prediction with better execution by the downstream system. The paper's contribution is therefore a way to refine an existing predictor around the particular aspects of motion that matter for action, rather than relying on overall future plausibility alone.
icml-2026-dyn-vpp-video-prediction-polic.tldr: Dyn-VPP post-trains diffusion video predictors with policy optimization to improve manipulation-relevant dynamics and downstream task success.

paragraphs: Recurrent-depth language models increase computation by applying layers repeatedly. This gives them an opportunity to refine internal representations through additional passes. The paper studies their relationship to diffusion language models and uses that connection to design a generation procedure that better exploits parallel computation.

The proposed diffusion forcing sampler decodes new tokens on every forward pass while continuing to refine token latent states through recurrence. Multiple positions can therefore receive updates in parallel. Under a fixed wall-clock budget, the authors prove greater expressivity than baseline autoregressive generation: the sampler maintains recurrent depth while updating a strictly wider set of token positions at equal serial depth.

The sampler applies directly to existing 3.5-billion-parameter recurrent-depth transformers without tuning, and the authors report speedups of up to five times. The result shows that the generation schedule itself can unlock additional efficiency from an already trained architecture. Its theoretical advantage is specifically tied to the budgeted comparison, while the measured speedup describes the evaluated model applications.
icml-2026-efficient-parallel-samplers-fo.tldr: A diffusion-inspired sampler generates new tokens while refining multiple positions in parallel, speeding existing recurrent-depth transformers by up to five times.

paragraphs: Binary logistic regression can receive either the true probability of each outcome or a sampled binary label. This paper shows that the distinction changes which algorithms work well, even when the underlying probability function has a simple form. In the studied over-constrained setting, noiseless soft labels suffice to recover the target weights and achieve Bayes risk.

With sampled hard labels and an s-sparse target in d dimensions, rotation-invariant algorithms incur excess risk of at least order (d−1)/n. Such algorithms do not favor a particular coordinate system. By comparison, simple algorithms that are sensitive to coordinates achieve an upper bound of order s log(d)/n, exploiting the target's sparsity.

Gradient descent on logistic loss, including early stopping, is an example of the rotation-invariant class. A successful alternative represents each weight as a product of two trainable parameters and performs gradient descent on those factors. The result isolates how label sampling interacts with algorithmic bias: for sparse targets, coordinate-sensitive parameterization can provide a substantially better statistical rate.
icml-2026-hard-labels-sampled-from-spars.tldr: For sparse logistic targets with sampled hard labels, rotation-invariant algorithms have worse excess-risk rates than simple coordinate-sensitive alternatives.

paragraphs: Generating samples with a diffusion model requires numerically solving a differential equation. Standard discretization approaches can need many small steps to achieve high accuracy. Previous iteration bounds grow polynomially with both the ambient dimension and inverse error tolerance, making increasingly accurate sampling theoretically expensive.

This paper introduces a solver that combines low-degree approximation with a collocation method. The authors prove that the number of iterations grows only polylogarithmically with inverse accuracy. That changes how rapidly the iteration requirement increases as the requested error shrinks. The guarantee uses approximate access to the data distribution's scores, rather than requiring exact scores.

The complexity bound also avoids an explicit ambient-dimension term. Dimension can still influence the result through the effective radius of the target distribution's support, so the claim has a specific geometric qualification. Together, these properties give a theoretical route to high-accuracy diffusion sampling whose iteration count depends much more mildly on precision and captures dimensional effects through the distribution's effective extent.
icml-2026-high-accuracy-and-dimension-fr.tldr: A new diffusion solver achieves polylogarithmic iteration dependence on inverse accuracy, with dimensional effects entering only through an effective support radius.

paragraphs: Energy-based models offer a flexible way to represent data distributions, but training them stably and efficiently remains difficult. This paper develops a cooperative approach that brings together an energy model, informative target latent variables, and a generator. The goal is to learn both the distribution of observations and meaningful relationships between observations and latent representations.

The latent variables guide a joint energy over data and latent information. A cooperating generator supplies effective initial states for Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling. Although optimization involves the joint space, the method requires MCMC sampling only in data space. The energy can therefore learn semantic data–latent relationships directly from real examples.

Experiments show improved generation quality and training stability with fewer resources, alongside effective performance on multiple downstream tasks. These findings support the proposed division of responsibilities: latent guidance helps organize what the energy learns, while the generator helps initialize sampling. The contribution combines those roles into one training framework aimed at making expressive energy-based modeling more practical.
icml-2026-latent-guided-cooperative-ener.tldr: Latent guidance and a cooperating generator improve energy-based model training while requiring MCMC sampling only in data space.

paragraphs: A learned feature can activate for scattered, unrelated inputs, making its meaning difficult to interpret. This paper proposes coherence as a geometric requirement for representations. Samples should attend to clustered features, and features should respond to clustered samples, with every sample represented and every feature serving some sample.

The authors prove that coherent non-negative matrices connect the topological structure of sample space and feature space through a bounded interleaving of their Vietoris–Rips filtrations. In more intuitive terms, the two spaces have compatible shape across scales. For data arranged on a circle, coherent features must cover contiguous arcs instead of unrelated scattered points.

To encourage this structure during training, the paper introduces Coh, a differentiable objective based on Fréchet variance. Sparsity restricts how many samples activate a feature; coherence also constrains which samples belong together geometrically. Evaluations use autoencoders on synthetic and rotated MNIST data and a BERT token embedding on language data. The aim is interpretability of both individual features and their collective organization.
icml-2026-learning-coherent-representati.tldr: A coherence objective encourages features to represent connected regions of data and gives sample and feature spaces compatible topological structure.

paragraphs: World models predict how actions change an environment, but collecting explicit action annotations can be difficult at scale. Latent action models learn an action representation from videos instead. This paper studies that approach on diverse in-the-wild videos, where environmental noise and the absence of a shared body or agent make action learning harder.

The authors examine how latent actions should be designed and evaluated. They find that constrained continuous representations suit these complex videos better than vector quantization. Learned actions can capture events such as a person entering a room and transfer those events across videos. However, without common embodiment, the learned actions are spatially localized relative to the camera.

The paper also trains a controller that translates known actions into the learned latent representation. This lets the latent space serve as an interface for planning, achieving performance on par with action-conditioned baselines in the reported tasks. The findings show both the reach of video-only action learning and the camera-relative structure that emerges from heterogeneous visual experience.
icml-2026-learning-latent-action-world-m.tldr: World models trained on diverse videos learn transferable latent actions that support competitive planning, though those actions remain camera-relative without shared embodiment.

paragraphs: A reinforcement learning policy can lose performance when deployment dynamics differ from training dynamics. Distributionally robust reinforcement learning addresses this by optimizing worst-case performance within a specified uncertainty set. Existing approaches often depend on strong access to data or focus on tabular problems, limiting their scope.

The paper introduces an online algorithm that learns directly through interaction, without prior knowledge or pre-collected data. It uses a dual-based fitted robust Bellman update to learn both the value function and the robust backup operator. General function approximation allows the method to represent these quantities beyond a table of individual states and actions.

The authors establish a sublinear regret bound for general phi-divergence uncertainty sets. The bound depends on an intrinsic measure called the robust Bellman–Eluder dimension, rather than directly on the number of states or actions, and recovers sharp rates in structured settings. The guarantee ties learning difficulty to the problem's functional complexity while preserving the focus on robustness within the chosen uncertainty set.
icml-2026-online-robust-reinforcement-le.tldr: An online robust reinforcement learning algorithm learns through interaction and achieves sublinear regret governed by intrinsic functional complexity.

paragraphs: A reconstructed CT image is an estimate, and its apparent detail does not by itself explain how confident one should be in that estimate. This paper builds confidence regions for CT reconstruction using sequential likelihood mixing. The regions have theoretical coverage guarantees, providing a principled way to describe uncertainty around reconstructed images.

The analysis uses a measurement model based on the Beer–Lambert law, with a log-linear forward relationship and Poisson noise. This connects the confidence framework to imaging conditions relevant to clinical and scientific use. The method applies across classical reconstruction algorithms and deep approaches, including U-Nets, ensembles, and diffusion models.

Empirically, deep reconstruction methods produce substantially tighter confidence regions than classical methods while retaining the theoretical coverage guarantees. The framework also supports hallucination detection and interpretable confidence visualizations. These results show how stronger reconstruction methods can contribute to more informative uncertainty estimates, with the guarantees grounded in the stated measurement model rather than the visual plausibility of an image alone.
icml-2026-principled-confidence-estimati.tldr: A CT confidence framework gives theoretical coverage guarantees and finds tighter confidence regions for deep reconstructions while supporting hallucination detection.

paragraphs: When language model agents collaborate, one agent's generated text often becomes another agent's input. Processing that shared content again creates redundant prefill computation, increasing memory use and time before the next agent produces its first token. RelayCaching aims to reuse work already performed while the earlier agent generated the text.

The method transfers decoding-phase key-value caches into subsequent prefill phases without additional training. Its central observation is that caches for identical content are highly consistent across these phases. Differences caused by the surrounding prefix are sparse and concentrated in limited layers and token positions, so selective recomputation can correct them with modest overhead.

Across collaborative tasks involving mathematics, general knowledge, and code generation, RelayCaching reuses more than 80% of the KV cache. It reduces time to first token by up to a factor of 4.7 compared with the standard pipeline, with negligible accuracy degradation. The result makes cache reuse more flexible by correcting localized differences instead of requiring every reused entry to remain unchanged.
icml-2026-relaycaching-accelerating-llm-.tldr: RelayCaching selectively repairs and reuses caches from earlier agents, reducing repeated processing with negligible accuracy degradation in evaluated collaboration tasks.

paragraphs: Reinforcement learning post-training can improve explicit reasoning in multimodal models while also weakening safety alignment. SafeThink addresses this at inference time by monitoring the developing reasoning trace. It treats safety as a threshold to satisfy, rather than an objective to maximize continuously throughout generation.

A safety reward model checks the trace, and SafeThink inserts a short optimized corrective prefix only when the safety threshold is violated. This conditional intervention aims to redirect generation while preserving the model's reasoning performance. The approach changes the generation process rather than requiring another round of model training.

Evaluations cover six open-source multimodal reasoning models and four jailbreak benchmarks. Reported examples include attack success falling from 63.33% to 5.74% and from 69.07% to 5.65%, while MathVista accuracy changes from 65.20% to 65.00%. An empirical finding is that intervention within the first one to three reasoning steps typically suffices to redirect the full response safely. This supports early, limited steering in the tested settings.
icml-2026-safety-recovery-in-reasoning-m.tldr: SafeThink conditionally steers early reasoning steps to reduce jailbreak success while largely preserving reasoning performance in the reported evaluations.

paragraphs: A distribution can be a mixture of individually manageable components while remaining difficult to analyze as a whole. This paper studies mixtures whose components satisfy approximate tensorization of entropy, or ATE. Although ATE helps with sampling and testing for individual distributions, even a mixture of a few such components need not satisfy it globally.

The first result establishes fast mixing of Glauber dynamics from a data-based initialization, with optimal sample complexity, for mixtures of distributions satisfying modified log-Sobolev inequalities. The initialization condition matters: the guarantee uses data to start the sampling process. This extends related work based on the weaker Poincaré inequality.

The second result gives efficient identity testers for mixtures of ATE distributions. These operate with coordinate-conditional sampling access, a specified form of access to the distribution. Together, the results show that useful sampling and testing guarantees can survive even when a mixture loses the global functional property of its components. This addresses a theoretical obstacle associated with multimodal distributions.
icml-2026-sampling-and-identity-testing-.tldr: Component-level functional inequalities suffice for new mixture sampling and identity-testing guarantees even when the full mixture lacks ATE.

paragraphs: Neural collapse describes an organized geometry in classifier features and weights. Previous theory linked lower-rank alternatives in deep architectures to explicit L2 regularization. This paper removes regularization and studies a deep unconstrained feature model, equivalent to a deep linear network with orthogonal inputs, to isolate the effects of depth and gradient descent.

The authors show that depth itself creates an implicit preference for low-rank solutions because low-rank matrices propagate norm more efficiently through repeated multiplication. They argue that the resulting alternatives correspond to softmax codes, max-margin configurations previously associated with width bottlenecks. Under spectral initialization, early repulsion among singular values helps drive the emergence of low rank.

The analysis also characterizes how increasing depth shrinks neural collapse's basin of attraction. Width can push in the other direction: with random initialization, wider networks favor higher-rank solutions. These results explain competing architectural influences on learned geometry within the studied model, providing both long-run and training-dynamics characterizations without attributing the effect to explicit regularization.
icml-2026-the-implicit-bias-of-depth-fro.tldr: In deep unconstrained feature models, depth implicitly favors low-rank alternatives to neural collapse, while increased width can favor higher rank.

paragraphs: Whole-slide pathology images are so large that processing many high-magnification patches becomes expensive. Standard multiple instance learning methods extract patch features and aggregate them into a slide-level prediction. PathCTM instead treats inference as a sequence of information-gathering decisions, determining where and at what scale additional inspection is useful.

The model starts with low-magnification global information and progressively moves toward higher-magnification local regions. Conditional computation controls scale changes, attention guides the removal of regions from further consideration, and confidence-aware early stopping ends inference once sufficient evidence has accumulated. These mechanisms adapt the amount of image processing to the evolving decision.

Compared with standard multiple instance learning methods, the reported experiments reduce required image patches by 95.95% and inference time by approximately 95.62%, without degradation in AUC. The result suggests that selective movement between scales can preserve predictive performance while avoiding much of the exhaustive patch processing. Its efficiency comes from deciding what evidence to inspect and when further inspection is unnecessary.
icml-2026-thinking-in-scales-acceleratin.tldr: PathCTM adaptively inspects pathology slides across scales, cutting patch use and inference time by about 96% without reported AUC degradation.

paragraphs: Matrices associated with overparameterized classification networks often have spectra with a large bulk and a smaller set of outlying directions. These low-dimensional patterns appear in several places, including weights, gradients, and the Hessian. The paper seeks a common analytic explanation instead of treating each matrix's spectral behavior separately.

Using unconstrained feature models, the authors connect these patterns to deep neural collapse. Within their analysis, the relevant eigenvalues and eigenvectors can be constructed from feature means, which characterize that collapse geometry. This explains both the strengths of spectral directions and their orientations, extending beyond descriptions that concentrate only on eigenvalue distributions.

The authors prove results for linear and ReLU networks within the modeling framework and provide numerical validation in both that framework and standard deep architectures on canonical datasets. The contribution is a shared account of several spectral phenomena through feature geometry. The numerical results also connect the analytic model to observed network behavior, rather than leaving the explanation entirely within an idealized setting.
icml-2026-unifying-low-dimensional-spect.tldr: An unconstrained-feature analysis links low-dimensional spectra across weights, gradients, and Hessians to the geometry of deep neural collapse.

paragraphs: Training transformers on long sequences often requires distributing context-related computation across accelerators. Existing context-parallel methods make this possible, but activation memory can still limit sequence length. Other techniques extend context further at a cost to training throughput, creating a practical trade-off between memory capacity and speed.

UPipe addresses this with fine-grained chunking at the level of attention heads. By organizing self-attention computation into smaller headwise pieces, it substantially reduces peak activation memory. The method targets the intermediate information retained during computation, enabling longer sequences while matching the training speed of previous context-parallel approaches in the reported comparisons.

For 70-billion-parameter transformers, the authors report peak activation memory reductions of up to 82.5%. For an 8-billion-parameter model on a single node with eight H100 accelerators, UPipe supports training contexts of up to five million tokens, a 25% improvement over prior methods. These results show that the organization of distributed attention computation can materially extend context capacity without the reported throughput penalty.
icml-2026-untied-ulysses-memory-efficien.tldr: UPipe chunks attention computation by head to reduce activation memory and extend training context lengths while matching previous context-parallel training speeds.
